newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's Lee knocks Western media on Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's Lee knocks Western media on Hong Kong.

text.p: Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew said the freedom of Western media to attack China with impunity from Hong Kong would not continue unimpeded, the Straits Times reported on Wednesday.

"You can't use a part of China to keep on every day throwing poison darts at Chinese leaders. They've got to make up their minds, either they accept certain realities or they will face a very unfriendly government," the newspaper quoted Lee as telling Singapore reporters in Hong Kong on Tuesday.
Talking about media coverage of Britain's handover of Hong Kong to China this week, Lee said journalists from the West were mainly looking for a story to support what they had been saying.

"You know, that Hong Kong is in grave danger, democracy is at stake, there will be no freedom of the press, civil liberties will go, civic society will be cramped and restricted. So, if they don't follow up on that story, they will be disappointed."

That meant there would be coverage of some of the protests, he said. "But if you look carefully, from what I saw on television, the protesters were very sparse, the banners and posters were very prosaic."
Lee was also quoted as saying Western media would learn in one to three years that most Hong Kong people were not overly concerned about democracy and human rights,
"We should make sure we get the message across that, by and large, the country expects to continue as before," he said.
Hong Kong's new leader Tung Chee-hwa views Lee, Singapore's firm-handed prime minister from 1959 to 1990, as one of the people he most admires. Lee wound up an 11-day visit to Hong Kong on Tuesday.
